title: The Signal Tower

beats.narrativeText: With much of Outpost Echo operational again, Atlas identifies one remaining communications structure: the Signal Tower.
The tower was intentionally shut down by the original expedition, for reasons not yet clear.
The learner inspects the tower's systems and identifies multiple engineering faults.
Diagnosing the faults reveals just how many separate problems must be solved before the tower can safely transmit.
The learner must develop a repair sequence, prioritising which faults to fix first.
Testing and refining each solution, the learner brings the tower back online.
The learner records the design decisions made throughout this first multi-stage engineering investigation.
Long-range communications become possible, and the learner discovers the expedition expected someone to return one day.

activities.title: Inspect Tower Systems
activities.storyContext: The Signal Tower was intentionally shut down by the original expedition.
activities.instructions: Inspect the tower's systems and note anything that looks damaged or disconnected.
activities.output: A list of observed issues with the tower's systems.

activities.title: Identify Faults
activities.storyContext: Before the tower can safely transmit, every fault must be diagnosed.
activities.instructions: Diagnose the specific engineering faults preventing the tower from working.

activities.title: Develop a Repair Sequence
activities.storyContext: This is the learner's first multi-stage engineering investigation, with no single prescribed approach.
activities.instructions: Decide the order in which the faults should be repaired, and explain why.

activities.title: Test and Refine Solutions
activities.storyContext: Each repair must be tested before moving on to the next.
activities.instructions: Test each proposed solution and refine it if it doesn't fully solve the fault.
activities.output: Tested and refined solutions for each fault.

activities.title: Record Design Decisions
activities.storyContext: A good engineer can always explain why they made the choices they did.
activities.instructions: Record the design decisions made throughout the repair, and the reasoning behind them.
activities.output: A written record of design decisions.

activities.title: Compare Alternative Repair Strategies
activities.storyContext: There is often more than one way to solve an engineering problem.
activities.instructions: Compare a couple of alternative repair strategies and justify the one you chose.
activities.output: A comparison of alternative repair strategies with a justified choice.

activities.title: Communication Towers in Remote Environments
activities.storyContext: Outpost Echo's Signal Tower faces the same challenges as real communication towers in remote places.
activities.instructions: Find out how communication towers operate in remote environments.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What was the hardest fault to fix, and how did you solve it?

discussionPoints: Why was it important to fix the faults in a particular order?
What did testing reveal that planning alone couldn't?
parentGuide.preparation: Simple building or craft materials are useful if the learner wants to model any part of the tower.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a repair sequence that is justified by reasoning, and evidence of testing and refinement across multiple faults.

completionCriteria: Tower faults identified, a repair sequence developed, and solutions tested and refined.
